stories.title: OpenAI rolls out GPT-5.6 after government greenlight — and announces ‘ChatGPT Work’
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: OpenAI has publicly rolled out GPT-5.6 following regulatory approval.
The rollout follows an initial limited preview restricted to government-approved organizations.
OpenAI also announced a new offering called 'ChatGPT Work' alongside the model update.

stories.title: OpenAI may have made a fatal misstep in copyright fight with news orgs
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: OpenAI faces potential sanctions regarding its handling of data in copyright litigation.
The core issue involves allegations that OpenAI hid or deleted ChatGPT usage logs during a copyright dispute with news organizations.
This highlights growing legal scrutiny over how large language models (LLMs) manage user data and intellectual property rights.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights a trending model, DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its primary function.
Tags suggest relevance to transformer architectures and conversational AI applications.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model from Meta.
It is featured on Hugging Face Benchmarks, indicating community interest and performance tracking.
The model is categorized under text-generation and utilizes standard ML frameworks like transformers.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-V4-Pro model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
It utilizes standard ML ecosystem components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance, measured by the Aider benchmark, shows speedups of up to 90%.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using its MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance gains.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware for optimized local AI inference.
The feature is currently available in a preview build, indicating ongoing development.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging apps with local AI coding agents.
The key feature is running all AI processes entirely on the user's own device for privacy/control.

stories.title: Google will now tell you if an ad was made with AI
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Google is implementing a new feature to disclose if ads on its platforms (Search, Discover, YouTube) were created or edited using AI.
The disclosure will appear in the 'My Ad Center' under the 'how this ad was made' tab.
This move signals a growing industry trend toward transparency regarding the use of generative AI in advertising.

stories.title: OpenAI wants its new tool to do your work for you and with you
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: OpenAI is developing a new tool, rebranded as Codex, aimed at automating and assisting user workflows.
The new capability suggests a move towards more autonomous AI agents capable of sustained, long-running tasks.
This signals a significant industry shift toward AI tools that function as independent, persistent collaborators rather than just single-query assistants.

stories.title: Humanoid robots controlled by surgeons did world-first operation on live pigs
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Humanoid robots are being tested in a preclinical surgical trial.
The robots performed a world-first operation on live pigs.
The research aims to assess the feasibility of robotic assistance in complex surgery.

stories.title: Breaking Database Lock-in: Agentic Regeneration of High Performance Storage Readers for Database Bypass
stories.author: Immanuel Trummer
bullet_points: Introduces 'Jailbreak,' a novel technique to bypass traditional database drivers (JDBC/ODBC) for data access.
Addresses a major bottleneck in analytical workloads by reading storage files directly instead of going through query execution layers.
Materializes data into in-memory columnar buffers to enable high-performance, bulk columnar analytics.

stories.title: Institutional Red-Teaming: Deployment Rules, Not Just Models, Causally Shape Multi-Agent AI Safety
stories.author: Yujiao Chen
bullet_points: Introduces 'institutional red-teaming,' a novel methodology to causally test the impact of deployment rules on multi-agent AI behavior.
The method isolates variables by fixing agents, objectives, and task state while systematically varying only one deployment rule.
Validated using IABench-CA, a large-scale benchmark spanning 228 contexts and seven model populations to assess rule efficacy.

stories.title: SkillCenter: A Large-Scale Source-Grounded Skill Library for Autonomous AI Agents
stories.author: Yushun Dong
bullet_points: Introduces SkillCenter, a large-scale, open skill library designed to provide grounded operational knowledge for autonomous AI agents.
The library boasts a massive scale, containing 216,938 structured skills across 24 domain bundles.
A key feature is the SkillGate-filtered pipeline, which curates 114,565 source-grounded skills from peer-reviewed and technical sources.

stories.title: Recursive Self-Improvement in AI: From Bounded Self-Refinement to Autonomous Research Loops
stories.author: Bo Qu
bullet_points: The paper surveys 1,250 arXiv papers to categorize the diverse concepts of AI self-improvement.
It critiques the current literature's tendency to conflate distinct ambitions under broad terms like 'self-refine' and 'self-evolve'.
The research analyzes how AI systems are moving toward autonomous research loops, improving their own behavior and policies.

stories.title: PALS: Percentile-Aware Layerwise Sparsity for LLM Pruning
stories.author: Alexey Shvets
bullet_points: PALS introduces Percentile-Aware Layerwise Sparsity to improve LLM pruning efficiency.
It dynamically adjusts per-layer sparsity based on activation magnitudes, unlike uniform methods like Wanda.
PALS significantly outperforms uniform pruning on LLaMA-2-7B, achieving lower perplexity (10.96 vs 12.92).

stories.title: GPT-5.6
stories.author: logickkk1
bullet_points: The news concerns the release or documentation of 'GPT-5.6' from OpenAI.
The provided links point to official OpenAI deployment safety documentation and API guides.
This suggests a significant update or iteration in OpenAI's flagship model offerings.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of 'subagents' for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: Microsoft’s carbon emissions went up 25 percent last year
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Microsoft's carbon emissions reportedly increased by 25 percent in 2025.
The increase was noted in Microsoft's 2026 sustainability report, suggesting challenges in meeting climate goals.
The rise in emissions was primarily attributed to the company's expansion.

stories.title: Fidji Simo steps down from leading OpenAI’s AGI work due to illness
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: OpenAI's AGI chief, Fidji Simo, is stepping down from her full-time role.
The transition is due to health reasons, following a previous announcement of medical leave for a neuroimmune condition.
Simo will continue to be involved with OpenAI as a part-time advisor.

stories.title: Netflix reportedly considers adding always-on channels
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Netflix is reportedly exploring the addition of always-on streaming channels.
This feature would allow continuous streaming of specific content, similar to Pluto TV or Tubi.
The key differentiator for Netflix would be its premium, ad-supported model, unlike the free, ad-supported competitors.

stories.title: The ChatGPT browser is already dead
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: OpenAI is discontinuing ChatGPT Atlas, its experimental browser feature.
Atlas, which aimed to perform tasks on the user's behalf, was launched less than a year ago.
The sunsetting of Atlas is part of a broader announcement regarding ChatGPT Work features.

stories.title: Microsoft’s patch Tuesdays are about to get bigger
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Microsoft is enhancing Patch Tuesday updates for Windows 11.
The company is integrating AI to proactively identify security vulnerabilities sooner.
This AI-driven approach will result in a higher volume of security fixes per release.

stories.title: Patch for Windows Defender 0-day could allow attackers to fill hard disk
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A vulnerability (0-day) in Windows Defender has been identified.
This vulnerability could potentially allow attackers to fill a hard disk.
The ongoing conflict between security researchers (NightmareEclipse) and Microsoft remains unresolved.

stories.title: Co-LMLM: Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Models
stories.author: Yoav Artzi
bullet_points: Introduces Co-LMLM (Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Models) as a new paradigm for LLMs.
LMLMs externalize factual knowledge to a Knowledge Base (KB) instead of memorizing it in model weights.
CO-LMLM specifically uses continuous keys to pair with textual knowledge values for dynamic retrieval.

stories.title: Selective Timestep Weighting and Advantage-Based Replay for Sample-Efficient Diffusion RLHF
stories.author: Soumik Mukhopadhyay
bullet_points: Addresses the sample inefficiency of applying Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) to diffusion models.
Proposes two complementary strategies: Selective Timestep Weighting and Advantage-Based Replay.
Aims to make diffusion RLHF more practical by reducing the dependency on large amounts of human or reward model evaluations.

stories.title: Agon: Competitive Cross-Model RL with Implicit Rival Grading of Reasoning
stories.author: Vladislav Beliaev
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in current Reinforcement Learning (RL) models where only the final answer is graded, leading to verbose but not necessarily better reasoning.
Introduces 'Agon,' a novel framework where two competing models act as each other's evaluators (graders).
The mechanism involves alternating roles: one model drafts a solution while the other critiques and solves it, aiming to improve the reasoning trace itself.

stories.title: DiaLLM: An Investigation into the Robustness-Generation Gap in English Dialect Adaptation
stories.author: Lu Yin
bullet_points: DiaLLM addresses the 'Robustness-Generation Gap' where LLMs understand dialects but fail to generate them.
The research involves continual pretraining of open-weight models using the International Corpus of English.
It compares various implicit/explicit post-training paradigms combined with different model alignment strategies.

stories.title: RL Post-Training Builds Compositional Reasoning Strategies
stories.author: Andrew Saxe
bullet_points: The research investigates whether Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training can enable models to compose primitive skills into novel, higher-level reasoning strategies.
The study uses a fully observable rewrite-grammar environment, allowing for complete auditing of generated reasoning steps.
A Transformer model pretrained on primitive symbol-rewrite chains is post-trained using RL on a trace-based reasoning task with a binary reward.

stories.title: Score Accuracy Along the Forward Diffusion Does Not Certify Numerical Stability in Diffusion Sampling
stories.author: Yiwei Zhou
bullet_points: The paper challenges the assumption that low forward-marginal error in diffusion models guarantees numerical stability during sampling.
It demonstrates that a smooth score field with small forward error can still lead to a nonexplosive and stable reverse-time process.
The research highlights a critical distinction between the error measured under forward marginals and the stability evaluated along the discrete sampling trajectory.

stories.title: SLORR: Simple and Efficient In-Training Low-Rank Regularization
stories.author: Shiwei Liu
bullet_points: SLORR introduces a new low-rank regularization technique for neural network compression.
It aims to overcome limitations of existing methods, such as reliance on SVDs or architectural modifications.
The proposed method is highlighted as being simple and stateless, suggesting easier implementation.

stories.title: Dimensionality Reduction Meets Network Science: Sensemaking on UMAP's kNN Graph
stories.author: Dominik Moritz
bullet_points: The paper explores the underutilized k-nearest-neighbor (kNN) graph constructed internally by UMAP.
This internal graph preserves the data manifold structure in the original high-dimensional space, unlike the final 2D projection.
Applying standard graph algorithms to this graph can enhance data sensemaking beyond typical UMAP usage.

stories.title: ARDY: Autoregressive Diffusion with Hybrid Representation for Interactive Human Motion Generation
stories.author: Davis Rempe
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical need for real-time, interactive 3D human motion generation.
It tackles the trade-off between offline methods (high control, slow inference) and online methods (fast inference, low control).
ARDY proposes a novel autoregressive diffusion model with hybrid representation to achieve both realism and interactive speed.

stories.title: Super Weights in LLMs and the Failure of Selective Training
stories.author: Akarsha Sehwag
bullet_points: Identifies 'Super Weights' in LLMs—individual parameters whose removal drastically impacts performance.
Challenges the assumption that Super Weights are universally critical across all LLMs.
Demonstrates that training these identified Super Weights in isolation severely degrades model accuracy, suggesting limitations in current pruning/training methodologies.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap where 3D pose estimation focuses on geometry, but real-world applications need biomechanical data.
A new lightweight plug-in temporal transformer, 'BioModule,' is proposed to bridge pose estimation and biomechanical attribute prediction.
The work has relevance across fields like rehabilitation, sports science, ergonomics, and clinical movement analysis.

stories.title: Latent Memory Palace: Reasoning for Control as Autoregressive Variational Inference
stories.author: Abhishek Gupta
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of transferring flexible, language-based reasoning capabilities from LLMs to continuous control policies.
Proposes a novel framework, 'Latent Memory Palace,' utilizing autoregressive variational inference to structure information for control.
Aims to bridge the gap between high-level linguistic reasoning and low-level, granular spatial/motor control.

stories.title: LTM: Large-scale Terrain Model for Wildfire-prone Landscapes
stories.author: Barath Raghavan
bullet_points: Addresses the critical need for accurate 3D terrain modeling in wildfire hazard assessment.
Proposes a multi-modal reconstruction framework to overcome limitations of expensive LiDAR and sparse image-based methods.
Focuses on improving terrain mapping accuracy over large, wildfire-prone landscapes.

stories.title: Co-LMLM: Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Models
stories.author: Yoav Artzi
bullet_points: Introduces Co-LMLM, a new paradigm for Limited Memory Language Models (LMLMs).
LMLMs externalize factual knowledge to a Knowledge Base (KB) instead of memorizing it in model weights.
CO-LMLM uses continuous keys in the KB to facilitate on-the-fly knowledge fetching during generation, offering better knowledge control.

stories.title: From Noisy Traces to Root Causes: Structural Trajectory Analysis and Causal Extraction for Agent Optimization
stories.author: Yuqing Yang
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenge of optimizing long-horizon agents that use LLMs for self-reflection and failure diagnosis.
Directly using raw execution traces for optimization is inefficient due to redundancy, heterogeneity, and irrelevant steps.
The proposed solution involves 'Structural Trajectory Analysis and Causal Extraction' to move from noisy traces to identifying root causes for better agent policy improvement.

stories.title: Agon: Competitive Cross-Model RL with Implicit Rival Grading of Reasoning
stories.author: Vladislav Beliaev
bullet_points: Introduces 'Agon,' a new framework for competitive cross-model Reinforcement Learning (RL).
Addresses a limitation in current reasoning models where RL only grades the final answer, leading to verbose but not necessarily better reasoning.
Agon uses two competing models where each acts as a grader for the other's solution, encouraging better reasoning traces.

stories.title: Does Bielik Know What It Doesn't Know? Activation Dispersion Separates Entity Familiarity from Factual Reliability Across Model Scale
stories.author: Grzegorz Brzezinka
bullet_points: The research investigates whether internal model activations can predict an LLM's familiarity with an entity before it generates an answer.
The study uses Polish Bielik models (1.5B-11B) to test entity familiarity across known, obscure, and fabricated entities.
A key finding suggests that activation dispersion may differentiate between entity familiarity and the factual reliability of the model's output.

stories.title: DiaLLM: An Investigation into the Robustness-Generation Gap in English Dialect Adaptation
stories.author: Lu Yin
bullet_points: Addresses the 'robustness-generation gap' where LLMs understand dialects but fail to generate them.
Introduces DiaLLM, a method involving continual pretraining on the International Corpus of English.
Compares various implicit/explicit post-training and model alignment strategies for dialect adaptation.

stories.title: RL Post-Training Builds Compositional Reasoning Strategies
stories.author: Andrew Saxe
bullet_points: The research investigates whether Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training enables models to compose latent primitive skills into novel, higher-level reasoning strategies.
The study uses a fully observable rewrite-grammar environment, allowing for auditing of every generated rewrite.
A Transformer model pretrained on primitive symbol-rewrite chains was post-trained using RL on a Trace-based reasoning task with a binary reward.

stories.title: Future Confidence Distillation in Large Language Models
stories.author: Sahil Kale
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical need for reliable confidence estimation when deploying LLMs in sensitive, confidence-aware systems.
Current methods often assess confidence only after the response is fully generated, ignoring the process.
This research proposes investigating confidence from a temporal perspective throughout the LLM's answering process.

stories.title: Postgres rewritten in Rust, now passing 100% of the Postgres regression tests
stories.author: SweetSoftPillow
bullet_points: A PostgreSQL implementation has been successfully rewritten in Rust.
The Rust rewrite has passed all existing PostgreSQL regression tests, indicating functional parity.
This represents a significant engineering effort in database technology, leveraging Rust's safety features.

stories.title: Announcing TypeScript 7.0
stories.author: devblogs.microsoft.com via evert
bullet_points: TypeScript 7.0 has been officially announced.
This release represents a significant update to the TypeScript language.
The announcement is being shared via the Lobsters community platform.

stories.title: Return on Attention: Why AI Code Reviews Are Wearing Us Out
stories.author: cseeman
bullet_points: AI code reviews are leading to increased PR volume without corresponding improvements in ticket quality.
The review process is increasingly automated, involving LLMs reviewing and responding to each other.
The core issue identified is broader than just code review, suggesting systemic problems in development workflows.

stories.title: An alternative to LLM quality gates: deterministic routing + sampling
stories.author: zxpmail
bullet_points: Challenges the core assumption of using LLMs to evaluate other LLMs (agent quality gates).
Proposes deterministic routing combined with sampling as an alternative evaluation method.
Addresses a known limitation in current LLM-based quality assurance pipelines.

stories.title: Everyone on the team is running agents. Nobody's running the same plan.
stories.author: henrypoydar
bullet_points: The article discusses the proliferation of AI agents within development teams.
While agent usage has led to an explosion in output, coordination issues are hindering actual results.
The core problem identified is a lack of standardized planning or coordination among autonomous agents.
